items.html: Greek licence plates are either all white or have the standard European design, with a blue strip on the left side. Taxis have yellow licence plates.

The Greek language features a unique alphabet not used in any other language. It shares similarities with both the Latin and Cyrillic alphabets, however the lower case letters generally have softer shapes than the Cyrillic letters.

NOTE: Cyprus also uses the Greek alphabet.
Greek utility poles are primarily wooden, and often have a distinctly dark brown colour. They will often be noticeably taller than in other countries.

These distinctive poletops, which have a metal frame shaped vaguely like a harp.

NOTE: They are unique to Greece and Cyprus.
Many poles in Greece will have five vertical insulators. They can either be attached to the pole or the metal frames from the previous tip.

This type of small lamp, attached to the side of poles with a round shade above the light bulb.

NOTE: You can also find them in North Macedonia and Serbia.
In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, solid white double middle lines. This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.
Yellow road lines are more common in Greece than any other southern European country.
Greek bollards are wedge-shaped with almost square reflectors, being red on the front and white on the back.

Greek chevrons have white arrows on a black background.

NOTE: Similar chevrons are found in Albania, Italy and the UK. Spain has the same colours, but will almost always have either two or four arrows.
Greek warning signs have a red border and a yellow background.

Greek directional signs are typically blue and arrow shaped. One of the most recognisable features are the place names, which are written in Greek with a yellow font, and in English with a white font.
Greek town entry signs are white with thick horizontal blue stripes at the top and bottom.
Greek kilometre markers are blue, having “km” written on the left in both the Latin and Greek alphabets.
Pedestrian signs have two dotted horizontal lines, rather than vertical stripes.
These types of miniature churches, put on small pedestals, are often found along Greek roads and are unique to Greece.

Greek architecture shares a lot of features with other Mediterranean countries: a lot of white and pastel-coloured stone houses with orange tiled roofs. White houses are very common when compared to most other Mediterranean countries.

Urban residential buildings will generally be multi-floored, light-coloured and typically have connected balconies along one or multiple walls.

Perhaps the most recognisable style of Greek architecture are the white houses with blue fences, window frames and doors. Beware that these are mainly found on islands.
Greece is a very mountainous country, with a large portion of the coverage being taken on winding mountain roads.

Red dirt is very common in Greece.

NOTE: Albania also has a lot of red dirt.

Greece has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front. The blur can also be fully transparent, making it harder to spot.
Greece has a lot of Generation 3 winter and fall coverage, which tends to look somewhat bleak and depressing.

Greece is a country with many small islands, some with coverage and some without. Furthermore, while mainland Greece and Crete have all three camera generations, this will not be true for most islands.

_You can click on the image to enlarge it._

Greek area codes will always begin with a 2, followed by 1-3 digits determining the area.

NOTE: If the third digit is 1, you will be in the largest city of the region, and if the third digit is 9, you will be in the area surrounding that city.

The largest flat agricultural valleys in Greece are found close to Thessaloniki and Larissa, but smaller flat valleys, where the mountains generally appear closer, can be found in several other areas in the north and centre of the country.
The tallest Greek mountains are found in the western half of the country, and contain most of the country’s high-altitude mountain roads with coverage.
One of the most well-known types of Greek architecture; houses with completely white walls, blue doors and shutters, is mainly found on the small central Cyclade islands.
On many of the central islands you can find a very barren landscape, with small bushes and no trees in sight. This tends to be more common on the smaller islands with coverage.
Olive plantations are found in coastal areas, particularly on Crete and southern Peloponnese.
Citrus plantations are mainly found in coastal areas, particularly on southern Peloponnese.
On Crete, you may find this unique car antenna, with a slight bulge at the tip.

Mount Pangaion can be recognised from its shape, being more of a solitary mountain rather than a wide mountain range, combined with the fact that it is located to the south of a flat agricultural valley.
These extraordinary monolithic mountains are called Meteora, and can be found north of Trikala.
Yellow taxis are found in Athens.
Blue taxis with a white roof are found in Thessaloniki.
In Thessaloniki, you will often see a large amount of unusually tall antennas on top of buildings.

lm.name: Agricultural Valleys
lm.note: The largest flat agricultural valleys in Greece are near Thessaloniki and Larissa. Smaller flat valleys, with mountains appearing closer, are found in other parts of the north and center.

lm.name: Aleppo Pine
lm.note: Aleppo pine grows across Central Greece and is typical in Attica and northern Euboea. It's also common in the Chalkidiki "fingers." Unlike Brutia pine, Aleppo often forms dense forests.

lm.name: Alexandreia Bins
lm.note: Alexandreia uses bins with Alexander the Great on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Argos Bins
lm.note: Argos uses bins with this design on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Athens Taxis
lm.note: Yellow taxis are found in Athens.

lm.name: Barren Landscape
lm.note:
On many of the central islands you can find a very

  • barren landscape
  • small bushes
  • no trees in sight This tends to be more common on the smaller islands with coverage.

lm.name: Chalkiadakis Supermarket
lm.note: Chalkiadakis supermarkets are unique to Crete. NOTE: On the stores there is not always a logo (only text).

lm.name: Chania Taxis
lm.note: Full dark blue taxis are found in Chania.

lm.name: Chios - Mastic Trees
lm.note: Mastic trees are very common in the southern part of the Chios island.

lm.name: Citrus Plantations
lm.note: Citrus plantations are mainly found in coastal areas, particularly on southern Peloponnese.

lm.name: Crete Antenna Bluge
lm.note: On Crete, you may find this unique car antenna, with a slight bulge at the tip.

lm.name: CRM Supermarket
lm.note: CRM Supermarkets can be seen in Macedonia and on Crete. Together with landscape this can be a useful clue.

lm.name: Cyclade Island Architecture
lm.note:
One of the most well-known types of Greek architecture; houses with

  • completely white walls
  • blue doors
  • and shutters Is mainly found on the small central Cyclade islands.

lm.name: Epirotic Architecture
lm.note: Grey stone houses with slate roofs are typical for Epirus, especially around Vikos Gorge in Pindus National Park. Even single grey stone houses are a good hint for this region.

lm.name: Fir Trees
lm.note: Unlike the Northern Pindus, in the Southern half of the Pindus range, fir trees are the dominant species.

lm.name: French Bollards
lm.note: A road from Kilkis to Kerkini Lake National Park (north of Thessaloniki) features French-style bollards, which are unique in Greece. Look at the map for exact locs.

lm.name: Greenhouses
lm.note: Large clusters of plastic greenhouses are common and effective in the Ierapetra area of southeastern Crete. Smaller greenhouse clusters also appear along other parts of Crete's southern coast.

lm.name: Heraklion Griffin Bins
lm.note: Heraklion uses bins with a griffin on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Jetoil Gasstations
lm.note: "Jetoil" gas stations are only seen in northern Greece. website with exact locs

lm.name: Komotini Bin
lm.note: Alexandreia uses bins with a sticker with 2 flowers on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Kos Bins
lm.note: Kos uses bins with a Tree or Flower on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Limnos Landscape
lm.note: Limnos has a unique, green landscape with few trees, many yellow flowers (likely dark mullein), and dense low bushes on hills.

lm.name: Macedonia-Thrace Bollards
lm.note: Within the Decentralised Administration of Macedonia and Thrace you will sometimes find these alternative bollards.

lm.name: Mani Architecture
lm.note: On the Mani peninsula in the Peloponnese you’ll find these unique stone towerhouses.

lm.name: Meteora Mountains
lm.note: These extraordinary monolithic mountains are called Meteora, and can be found north of Trikala.

lm.name: Mount Pangaion
lm.note: Mount Pangaion stands out as a solitary mountain rather than part of a wide range and is located just south of a flat agricultural valley.

lm.name: Mykonos Bins
lm.note: Mykonos uses bins with this design on them (also you can read "MYKONOY"). NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins on the Island

lm.name: Naousa Bins
lm.note: Naousa uses bins with a logo on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Olive Plantations
lm.note: Olive plantations are found in coastal areas, particularly on Crete and southern Peloponnese.

lm.name: Patras Bins
lm.note: Patras uses bins with a sticker on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Patras Taxi
lm.note: Patras uses (dark)-red taxis.

lm.name: Peach Trees
lm.note: Greece is the world’s 3rd largest producer of peaches, and these are heavily concentrated around the cities of Edessa and Veria, along with some other non-citrus fruit plantations.

lm.name: Pinus Nigra
lm.note: While the map shows several hotspots, the main areas with Pinus Nigra forests are at the northern end of the Pindus Mountains. The spots in the Peloponnese are also notable.

lm.name: Pistacchio Plantations
lm.note: The island of Egina is full of pistacchio plantations, which are relatively unique to the island.

lm.name: Rice
lm.note: Rice can only be seen in these two areas

lm.name: Russian Signs
lm.note: Heraklion is a popular holiday spot for Russians, and it is not uncommon to find signs written in Russian in the more touristic parts.

lm.name: Santorini Architecture
lm.note: Santorini architecture is very distinct. Like cyclade architecture more generally, it is very whitewashed, however it is distinct for its curved roofs and semi-circle windows/porticoes.

lm.name: Slate Slabs
lm.note: Some houses on Ikaria have these distinct roofs made of large slate slabs.

lm.name: Sunflowers
lm.note: Sunflower plantations are most common in the far northeast corner of the country and generally restricted to the north of the country.

lm.name: Synka Supermarket
lm.note: Synka supermarkets are unique to Crete (especially west).

lm.name: Tall Mountains
lm.note: The tallest Greek mountains are found in the western half of the country, and contain most of the country’s high-altitude mountain roads with coverage.

lm.name: Thessaloniki Antennas
lm.note: In Thessaloniki, you will often see a large amount of unusually tall antennas on top of buildings.

lm.name: Thessaloniki Bins
lm.note: Alexandreia uses bins with stylised thetas (θ)** on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Thessaloniki Taxis
lm.note: Blue taxis with a white roof are found in Thessaloniki.

lm.name: Veria Bins
lm.note: Veria uses bins with two coins on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.name: Volos Ship Bins
lm.note: Volos uses bins with a ship and the greek name ("Βόλος") on them. NOTE: You will find other kinds of bins in this city

lm.note: These distinctive poletops, which have a metal frame shaped vaguely like a harp, are unique to Greece.

lm.name: lamp with a round shade

This type of small lamp, attached to the side of poles with a round shade above the light bulb.

NOTE: You can also find them in North Macedonia and Serbia.

lm.name: wooden pole top
lm.note: In Greece you will finde a lot of these wooden crossbar.

lm.name: Athens street sign
lm.note: Athens has this street sign with an extra part under the main street sign.

lm.name: Athens taxi
lm.note: Yellow taxis with a blue stripe around the taxi are found in Athens.
